description:
FILED s473t4 (#1501 CHECK 1 round 1, 2026-09-13).  t/op/goto.t is TRANSPILE-FAIL: P 132/2, C 0/0 -- the whole file, 134 rows.

    $ ./pl2cl < t/op/goto.t
    Parser2 TODO: my-lexical 'count' (canon $count) spans a package boundary

BISECTED (binary search over line prefixes) to the FIRST failing prefix, t/op/goto.t:271.  The two declarations in that prefix:
    85:  my $count = 0;                 <- file level
    231:     my $count;                 <- inside `package Do_undef { â¦ }` (line 230)
    271: for ($count=0; $count<2; $count++) {    <- file level again, the FILE-level one

MINIMAL REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):
    use strict; use warnings;
    my $count = 0;
    $count = 7;
    package Do_undef {
        my $count;
        sub bump { $count++; return $count }
    }
    print "file=$count inner=", Do_undef::bump(), "\n";
    perl: file=7 inner=1
    pcl : Transpile failed: Parser2 TODO: my-lexical 'count' (canon $count) spans a package boundary

These are TWO different variables in perl: the inner `my $count` is scoped to the package BLOCK and the file-level `$count` after it is the one declared at the top.  PCL's resolver canonicalises both to `$count` and then refuses because the one name is seen inside and outside a package region.

RELATED, and probably the same resolver: #475 (a FILE-level `our` alias is not requalified across a TOP-level `package` statement).  The distinguishing measurement is cheap -- probe the `package NAME;` (statement) spelling of the same reproducer beside the `package NAME { }` (block) one before designing; only the BLOCK spelling was measured here, and the block spelling ALONE (a package block with a `my $x` and no file-level `my $x`) transpiles fine, so the refusal is about the PAIR, not about either declaration.

SIZE: the whole of op/goto.t (134 rows) is behind it.  Round t5a.

=== DONE (s473t5a, 2026-09-13) ===

FIXED, and the diagnosis in the filing was right about the PAIR but wrong about
where the pair is decided.  The span CHECKER (`_check_my_spanning`) was already
correct: it SKIPS a block-form package segment's declarations ("its `my`s die
with the block"), so it never thought the two `$count`s were one variable.  What
refused was the span RENAME (`_rename_spanning_lexicals`): the file-level
`$count` genuinely SPANS (segment 2 reads it), the rename would have promoted
it, and its eligibility gate counted the block's `my $count` as a same-level
re-declaration -- `SPANREFUSE count@seg0: sdecls=2 dc=2` -- after which the
checker killed the file.

WHY THE COUNT WAS WRONG, and the general lesson: `_hard_decl_count`'s own rule
is "a decl nested inside a `Structure::Block` or a named sub is a scopeable
SHADOW, not a same-level re-binding".  A `package Foo { my $x; … }` decl IS
inside a block -- but the segment FLATTENING hands those statements over as the
segment's TOP level, so by the time the count runs there is no block between
the declarator and the statement.  The compensation therefore has to be made at
the SEGMENT level, which is exactly where the checker, the span pre-filter and
the container pass already make it (three sites, same one-line rule).  This was
the fourth.

THE REWRITE NEEDED NOTHING.  A block-form segment's PPI parent IS the package
block, so `_ref_shadowed` already discounts every use the block's own decl
shadows, and `_symbol_is_declarator` skips the declarator itself.  Probed:
a use BEFORE the block's own `my` is rewritten to the promoted cell (perl reads
the outer variable there) and a use after it is left alone.  USE facts
(`$family`/`$interp`) are deliberately NOT segment-skipped: a block-form
segment that merely READS the outer lexical is a real reference.

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3, identical after and ALL FOUR refusing on a
`git archive 8c8fa4c0` extraction:
  - the filing's reproducer                                  file=7 inner=1
  - a block-form segment that only READS the outer lexical    in=4 after=4  (already OK before)
  - use before / after the block's own `my`                   pre=1 post=9 after=1
  - two block-form packages each declaring the same name      file=1 A=2 B=3
Guard: `Pl/t/transpile-test-09.t` row "my inside a package BLOCK is not the
file lexical (#1581)", four conjuncts in one snippet, inverse-verified.

THE `package NAME;` STATEMENT SPELLING, which the filing asked for: it is NOT
this bug and never was.  The refusal is specific to the BLOCK form, because
only the block form makes a segment whose `blockform` flag is set; the
statement form opens an ordinary segment whose `my` really does live to the end
of the file, and a same-name file lexical there is a genuine ambiguity the
existing `sdecls`/`dc` gate is right to refuse.  #475 (a FILE-level `our` alias
not requalified across a TOP-level `package` statement) is a different
mechanism and is untouched.

t/op/goto.t DOES NOT MOVE: the transpile now reaches a SECOND refusal,
"Parser2 TODO: forward goto to a standalone label", and the file stays
TRANSPILE-FAIL at 0 rows.  That residue is task #1654, which also records the
surprising part -- the same label transpiles at line-prefix 78 and refuses at
79, so a LATER standalone label un-marks an EARLIER one in the #63 catch-wrap.

Measured elsewhere: `tools/corpus-diff.pl` IDENTICAL over 111, so no file in
the corpus was relying on the refusal.
subject: A `my $x` inside a `package NAME { â¦ }` BLOCK makes a FILE-level `my $x` of the same name refuse: "my-lexical spans a package boundary" -- op/goto.t loses all 134 rows
